coverageNote.note: Westrock Coffee operates ~10 facilities (US + Rwanda + Tanzania for green-coffee sourcing). We audited 6 US sites.

account.dossierIntro: Westrock Coffee runs the largest US-based private-label coffee and extracts operation. 10 facilities; we audited 6. Conway AR DC has 72 dock doors. Conway AR Roast-to-RTD plant is 47 acres. 211 total dock doors. YardFlow runs the green-coffee inbound and finished-product outbound as two distinct queues on one yard graph.
surprisingFindings: Conway AR Roast-to-RTD plant is 47 acres of vertically integrated coffee operations.
211 dock doors across 6 audited sites. Westrock runs efficient dock density per SKU.
1 of 6 audited sites is rail-served. Inbound green coffee moves through containers, not rail.

caveats: Westrock Coffee - Conway AR Distribution Center: audit note mentions 'closed'
Westrock Coffee - Conway AR Single-Serve "Clark" Plant: audit note mentions 'closed'

sites.name: Westrock Coffee - Conway AR Roast-to-RTD Plant

steps.step: Arrive at gate (no guard, kiosk or call box)

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster supplied 35.073662, -92.416857 (ROOFTOP geocode, but the pin landed
on the NE construction/laydown corner of the property). Web research confirmed
this is the **former Kimberly-Clark Conway paper-products plant at 480 Exchange
Avenue**, which Westrock Coffee purchased and converted into North America's
largest roast-to-RTD beverage manufacturing facility — a $315M project, ~570,000
sq ft on a ~45-acre campus, grand opening June 2024 (Arkansas Business, Dairy
Foods, Westrock Coffee press release). Satellite probing confirmed a large
sprawling multi-section industrial complex consistent with a converted paper
mill. The center was locked to the main building mass at 35.0721, -92.4188.

fieldNotes.location: Confirmed as the former Kimberly-Clark Conway paper-products plant at 480 Exchange Avenue, now Westrock Coffee's roast-to-RTD facility ($315M, 570K sq ft, ~45 acres, opened June 2024). The roster pin sat at the NE construction/laydown corner; locked center moved SW to the main building mass at 35.0721,-92.4188.
fieldNotes.truckGate: A sliding chain-link gate across a truck driveway is clearly visible in 2024-08 Street View on the NE side of the property (near 35.0760,-92.4188), with continuous chain-link perimeter fencing running along the warehouse face. The truck/yard side of the campus is access-controlled.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth was positively identified at the truck gate in available imagery. The NE truck gate is a rolling chain-link gate with no adjacent booth visible — implying remote/kiosk check-in. A large former-paper-mill campus of this scale may have a manned gate elsewhere; marked uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Truck gate present, no guard shack seen — remote check-in inferred.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated trailer drop yard on the NE flank of the plant (wc-rtd-dropyard-z19) holding ~60-85 trailers parked in rows, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Drop yard rows visibly hold well over 50 trailers — banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock doors distributed across multiple building faces (NE drop-yard side and the SE face along I-40). ~30-45 doors estimated across the sprawling complex; exact count limited by roof complexity and scale — banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale site: a sprawling main manufacturing building plus several distinct ancillary/warehouse structures (NE warehouse, NW building, support buildings) within one fenced property.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the south edge of the property (visible in wc-rtd-sw); former Kimberly-Clark paper mills were rail-served and a spur appears to enter the site.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Very wide paved aprons and multiple driveways/access points give ample room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the Conway industrial fabric directly along Interstate I-40 with dense surrounding commercial/retail development — judged Urban.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Extensive paved internal yard provides holding/queue room inside the fence before the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The internal gate-to-dock approach is long and can stack 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified; marked uncertain given site scale.

is the Clark plant. Its footprint and trailer activity match a 525K sq ft
plant. The shell is already present in 2024 imagery — consistent with a

fieldNotes.location: Identified as the large gray-roof warehouse/manufacturing building on William J. Clark Drive immediately SOUTH of the Westrock DC. This is the 525,000 sq ft 'Clark' single-serve (K-cup pod) facility — 130,000 sq ft manufacturing plus fulfillment/distribution — that Westrock opened July 2025. The shell appears in 2024 imagery (likely a Tempus-developed spec building that Westrock fitted out and occupied in 2025). The roster pin (-92.409215) sat ~350m too far west on an unrelated older trucking yard; center re-locked to the gray building at 35.0578,-92.4050.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Continuous chain-link perimeter fencing surrounds the property (clearly visible in 2024-07 Street View along the south frontage and around the yard). A sliding chain-link gate across the truck driveway is visible at the NW/SW corner where the yard connects to William J. Clark Drive. The truck yard is fully enclosed.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth positively identified. The truck entrance reads as a sliding chain-link gate with no adjacent booth — implying kiosk/remote check-in. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Truck gate present, no guard shack seen — remote check-in inferred.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long banks of dock doors with trailers backed in along BOTH the north and south long faces of the building; ~50-70 doors estimated across the two faces — banded 50+. Exact count limited by imagery scale.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Trailer-parking lanes line both long faces with ~60-80 trailers present; a dedicated drop/storage function is clear (dropArea banded 50+).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Well over 50 trailers parked along the building's two dock faces.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks run on two physically separate building faces (north face and south face) — consistent with separate ship/receive flows; marked true but uncertain since both faces could serve mixed traffic.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide perimeter loop road and deep aprons give room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Deep gate-to-dock approach along the perimeter loop stacks 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved yard inside the fence provides holding/queue room before the docks.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Conway industrial corridor near I-40 with surrounding industrial development — Urban.
fieldNotes.imagery: Building opened operationally July 2025; available satellite/Street View predates full Westrock occupancy. Structure is fully built in imagery, so layout audit is reliable; operational specifics carry medium confidence.

sites.name: Westrock Coffee - North Little Rock AR Roasting & Manufacturing
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster geocode (ROOFTOP, moved 95 m) lands on the correct building. Web
search confirms "Westrock Coffee Company — Roasting & Manufacturing" at 30
Collins Industrial Pl, North Little Rock (Little Rock Chamber listing, Yelp,
Waze, joe.coffee, NAICS). This is Westrock's original/legacy private-label
roasting plant predating the new Conway campus.

The building is the white-roofed, L-shaped industrial structure on the south
side of Collins Industrial Place, inside the Collins Industrial Place
light-industrial subdivision. It is positively distinguished from neighbors by
its L footprint, its own front (north) employee/visitor parking apron, and the
roasting-plant dock arm on the southwest leg.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck entrance. The facility sits inside the multi-tenant Collins Industrial Place industrial park; satellite and 2024 Street View show open, unmarked driveways and shared paved aprons connecting buildings — no barrier arm, sliding gate, or pinch-point checkpoint at the property line.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth anywhere on the site or at the park access.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock doors are on the building's southwest arm; ~6-8 bays estimated with 3-4 trailers backed in (wc-04-sat-n imagery). Resolution and roof glare limit an exact count.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A few trailers stand near the SW dock arm; no large marked drop-stall lot belonging to Westrock. The big dirt lot full of trucks/RVs/salvage east of the building is a SEPARATE adjacent salvage/towing operation, not Westrock's yard.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town light-industrial subdivision in North Little Rock — judged Rural per the small-town-industrial rubric tiebreak.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Approach from the park drive to the dock arm is short (1-2 trucks).

sites.name: Westrock Coffee - Concord NC Roasting & Extract Campus (S&D legacy)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster geocode (ROOFTOP, moved 90 m) lands on the correct building cluster.
Web search confirms S&D Coffee & Tea / Westrock Coffee at 300 Concord Parkway
South, Concord NC — the legacy S&D headquarters and primary custom-roasting and
iced-tea/extract complex, in operation since 1927 and acquired by Westrock
Coffee. CoPack Connect, Dun & Bradstreet, Encyclopedia.com and Panjiva buyer
records all tie 300 Concord Parkway South to S&D Coffee roasting operations.

The site is the large multi-building industrial campus on the NW side of
Concord Parkway South. It is distinguished from the unrelated big-box retail
and car dealership on the opposite (SE) side of the parkway, and from idx 6
(101 Commercial Park Dr SW, ~0.4 mi SW — a separate building).

fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm or sliding gate found at the truck entrance off the campus drive. The truck yard is reached by a curved private campus drive from Concord Parkway South; satellite shows wide open paved aprons and no checkpoint pinch-point. Some campus drives off Concord Pkwy could not be Street-Viewed at the actual yard entrance (2017/2026 panos cover the highway frontage and the across-road dealership side), so this is marked uncertain — but no gate structure is visible in overhead imagery.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth visible at the yard entrance or along the campus drive.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Long dock apron on the NE face of the north building shows ~14 trailer/dock positions in the close-up, plus additional bays around the building cluster — ~22 estimated site-wide. Multi-building campus makes an exact total hard to confirm.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of ~4 connected/adjacent large buildings — the legacy S&D Coffee & Tea main roasting-and-extract complex.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Trailers parked in a yard area NW of the dock apron, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved yard aprons and ample maneuvering width — physical room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Located on Concord Parkway South, a busy multi-lane signalized arterial within the Charlotte-metro fabric (apartments, big-box retail, dealerships adjacent) — Urban.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved yard between the campus entrance and the dock doors gives interior holding room.

Commercial Park Drive industrial subdivision, against a wooded edge to the south
and east. It is ~0.4 mi southwest of idx 5 (300 Concord Parkway South). The two
are confirmed distinct buildings: idx 5 is the multi-building roasting campus on
the parkway; idx 6 is a single warehouse on the Commercial Park loop. They were

fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck entrance. Multiple Street View captures (2019, 2020, 2023, 2026) of Commercial Park Drive SW and the building's dock side show open driveways, no barrier arm, no sliding gate, and no checkpoint pinch-point. The only fencing seen is a small chain-link enclosure around process/utility equipment on the building flank — not a perimeter or gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth visible at the entrance or anywhere on the parcel.

fieldNotes.locationDisambiguation: Roster geocode for this address moved 1693 m. The building was independently verified at 101 Commercial Park Drive SW (Waze, BusinessYab, Panjiva 'S&D Tea Annex' buyer records) — a distinct facility ~0.4 mi SW of idx 5 (300 Concord Pkwy S).
